title: A ritual without completing every detail

captions.energy: Demanding the entire form be fulfilled

meaning: Shared pleasure benefits from permission to shorten a familiar form when completing the whole ritual turns participation into mutual accounting.
text: A familiar pleasure can quietly acquire overly detailed conditions. The Hierophant in the physical position of Svadhisthana describes participating in a shared tradition: repeating the arrangement, performing known actions and joining a recognisable activity. The World in energy leans towards complete fulfilment, as though a shortened version did not count as proper leisure. Justice in emotions assesses fairness: who prepared more and who received enjoyment. Tradition provides support, the demand for completeness increases effort, and fairness can turn a small ritual into an account of responsibilities between two people.

Suppose you usually draw amusing cards for each other at the month’s end. Time is short today, yet the drawing, lengthy message and attractive wrapping all seem necessary. **A shortened tradition can remain a complete shared pleasure.** One funny sketch already provides a reason to meet and smile. Participation need not involve equal work to be voluntary; you can agree which version suits you both now.

The difficulty is restoring fairness by requiring every detail to be completed equally. The evening goes into proving effort, with enjoyment waiting behind an inspected result. Different capacities start looking like different feelings. A shared form helps while its scale can change. Fairness can lie in freely agreed relief, beyond precise equality in how many details each person managed to prepare and present.
